text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** The pages I found agree on this, though I only had their search snippets and didn't open them.

| | LiFePO4 (LFP) | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| **Cycle life** | About 3,000–6,000 cycles | About 1,000–2,000 cycles |
| **Safety** | More thermally stable and less prone to thermal runaway | Needs more careful thermal management |
| **Weight and size** | Heavier and bulkier | About 20% lighter per Wh |
| **Cost** | Usually costs a bit more per unit, but is cheaper per cycle over its life | Often cheaper up front on older or budget models |
| **Cold weather** | Charging below freezing can damage cells unless the unit has heating | Tolerates cold charging a bit better |

The cycle-life and weight figures come from [PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc). The rest is general industry knowledge.

**Choose LFP if** you want it for home backup, RV or van use, camping, or daily use. It should last a decade or more, and it's safer to keep indoors.

**Choose NMC if** weight is your top priority, such as backpacking or frequent carrying, and you'll only use it occasionally. It can also make sense if you find a good deal on a lightweight unit.

LFP is becoming the default. [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc) notes that all 54 power stations in its data set use LiFePO4. [Unplugged Watts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/) also says LFP is the better buy for most people.
